A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SynGA/SynGBO research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original analog-search, molecular-property optimization and computational docking results, together with mutation, filtering and neural additive model ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds analog-search datasets, broader docking evaluations, runtime controls and search-space ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 change their stated return value from P to H, the archive of evaluated molecules and fitnesses. This is a limited pseudocode/output correction; the genetic operators, filtering models, losses and Bayesian optimization steps remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds analog-search evaluations on DDS-10 and ZINC; v1 used ZINC only to check oracle-version consistency. Docking expands from ALDH1, ESR_ant and TP53 to all 15 LIT-PCBA receptors. Appendix C.6 also evaluates additional Enamine building-block catalogs, substantially broadening the chemical search environments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained analog-search, PMO and docking experiments is unchanged. Added datasets and controls reuse existing comparators, including SynFormer, ChemProjector and 3DSynthFlow. The corrected name RGFN denotes the comparator called RFGN in v1.

E3.justification: New protocols include a 3.3k-call SynGA run with proportionally reduced initialization for approximate runtime matching, top-five analog diversity reporting, and search-space controls using 38 bimolecular templates, two reaction steps and 40 atoms. The ALDH1 mode-count caption also changes its docking threshold from <10 to <-10; unchanged result values do not establish rerunning.

E4.justification: Appendix B.5 adds a runtime-budget study testing whether analog quality survives reduced computation. Appendix C.6/Table 13 adds catalog and reaction-space ablations addressing search-space confounding. These introduce important controls beyond the retained mutation, filtering, random-search and NAM ablations.

E5.justification: The existing reporting practices remain: means and standard deviations over five seeds for PMO and related ablations, and four seeds for docking, with the same stated baseline exceptions. Added docking results follow that practice. No new uncertainty estimator, significance test or increase in repeated-run counts is reported.

E6.justification: Shared ChEMBL, PMO and three-receptor docking scores are retained, but substantial results are added. Table 9 reports SynFormer/SynGA reconstruction rates of 0.858/0.707 on DDS-10 and 0.558/0.459 on ZINC. V2 also adds reduced-budget results, search-space ablation outcomes, docking and ligand-efficiency results for twelve more receptors, and PMO optimization trajectories.

T1.justification: The synthesis-tree definitions and assumptions, NAM Equation 1, inverse-rank sampling derivation in Appendix A.3 and ranking-loss formulation remain unchanged. V2 introduces no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: synthesis-constrained genetic search, ML-guided block filtering, SynGBO, and competitive or state-of-the-art molecular optimization. The expanded evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 adds substantive applicability qualifications, explaining SynFormer's advantage through reconstruction training and distinguishing exact reconstruction from smoother analog projection. It hypothesizes different behavior on reachable versus out-of-distribution queries. Appendix C.6 newly attributes late-stage diversity deficits to GA exploitation versus reward-proportional sampling, substantially extending the interpretation of strengths and limitations.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the anonymous code location with a named GitHub repository and removes the promise of a future MLP-checkpoint release; checkpoint availability is not established by the PDFs. It documents catalog downsampling and the top-10k block filter used with the 1.2M catalog. Existing architecture, training and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Enamine diversity-libraries citation and refines its positioning against amortized projection methods through the SynFormer discussion in Appendix B.5. The background literature and central novelty positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. V2 adds a separate Section 3.4 heading for the existing SynGBO description, introduces Appendix B.5, expands C.6, corrects grammar and terminology, and updates the publication header. These are localized narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: V2 adds comparison/control tables and PMO optimization curves, gives Table 5 a mean column, adds full receptor-wise docking displays and expands the ligand-efficiency table. The ligand figures are reorganized from per-seed examples for three receptors into separate 15-receptor grids for SynGA and SynGBO, substantially changing the empirical presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evaluation of the existing method. The three-target docking study expands to all fifteen receptors, while runtime and search-space controls address important comparison confounds. DDS-10/ZINC results favoring SynFormer also establish clearer limits to SynGA's advantages. Runtime and catalog matching remain approximate, but the broader evidence, added controls and more balanced interpretation materially improve the support for the paper's conclusions.
